validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and correctly classified. The gem.wiki page's citation pool for this row is entirely generic (A Barrel Full = banned; the old fgttransfer.energytransfer.com system-map link 404s; eia.gov/maps/layer_info-m.php is a GIS-layer index, not a value source; kindermorgan.com/.../FGT/default.aspx 404s; fractracker.org and oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491 are whole-system pages, not this phase specifically) EXCEPT the eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php citation, which is itself a navigation page per the sweep's own rule -- so per se none of the 9 harvested citations name this specific phase. I did not stop there: the data.php page links to EIA's downloadable 'U.S. Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook, which itself is FERC-authority government data, independent of GEM and of the wiki. I pulled the Jan-2023 edition directly (https://www.eia.gov/naturalgas/pipelines/EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Jan2023.xlsx) and its 'Historical Projects (1996-2022)' tab row 864 is an EXACT, independent match to this GEM row: Project Name 'Southwest Alabama Project', Operator 'Florida Gas Trans Co', Type 'Expansion', Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2022-01-12, Year In Service 2022, States 'MS,AL' (Beg_State MS / End_State AL), Cost (millions) 2.2, Miles blank, Additional Capacity (MMcf/d) 100, Diameter blank, Authority FERC. That corroborates the sheet's Capacity=100 MMcf/d, SegmentCost=2,200,000 USD, StartYear1=2022, StartState/Province=Mississippi, EndState/Province=Alabama, Status=operating (a completed/in-service FERC expansion), and the blank Miles/Diameter in EIA affirmatively support GEM's LengthKnown=0.00/blank Diameter under the no-new-physical-pipe convention (this being a compression-only capacity addition, not a new lateral). CLASSIFICATION is correct: a distinct, FERC-authorized interstate expansion phase on the FGT system, gas commodity. DUPLICATE check against the 37-PID roster: no other roster row shares Capacity=100 MMcf/d or these specs, so no collision within this batch. Note for the record (not a GEM defect): the gem.wiki page itself misstates this project's cost as 'US$0.77 million' citing the same eia0421 reference -- that figure actually belongs to a DIFFERENT EIA row, 'FGT Alabama Power Lateral' (cost 0.77, capacity 62, diameter 12), a mix-up on the wiki page's part. GEM's own sheet value (2,200,000 USD) is the one that actually matches the EIA 'Southwest Alabama Project' row, so the sheet is correct where the wiki text is not -- this is not something to fix in GEM's data, just a heads-up that the wiki page (never cited by us) has a sourcing slip on this phase. CAVEAT: this is a SINGLE independent source (EIA), not the 2-independent target. I searched for a second, distinct origin -- the actual FERC certificate docket for this expansion -- but could not reach it: this session's WebSearch budget was exhausted (200/200) before I could search for the docket number; FERC's elibrary.ferc.gov is an Angular SPA that serves only the JS shell to a scripted client (no server-rendered search results or discoverable REST endpoint found); Bing and DuckDuckGo's non-JS/lite search endpoints returned bot-challenge pages or empty/irrelevant carousels to curl; Marginalia's indexed search returned zero hits. I also confirmed the wiki-cited Kinder Morgan FGT project page (kindermorgan.com/pages/business/gas_pipelines/east/FGT/default.aspx) is a dead 404, and could not find a live current Kinder Morgan FGT project-specific page. So tier is medium on the value cells despite the exact match, and every affected fills[] entry documents this same second-source search. Opened/read to exhaustion: the full EIA 2023 historical-projects tab (1,120 rows) for every 'Florida Gas Trans Co' row (18 found, logged), and the live gem.wiki page's Southwest Alabama Project section plus its citation-pool.
